Product proposal / not a deployed product surface

One boundary
at a time.

The machine runs locally. The proposed product layer earns its next capabilities through named contracts and acceptance gates, beginning with a reproducible local proof loop.

Read the product specification →

Delivery order

A / Contracts

Freeze schemas, threat models, canonicalization, verifier images, and evidence formats.

B / Local loop

Run one builder and three critics against a real wasm-vm workload, with replayable settlement and no required token.

C / Volumes

Prove credentials, recovery slots, encrypted generations, rotation, and revocation.

D / Delivery

Unify HTTP, cache, WebRTC, and torrent-like sources with demand-first reads and hash-before-cache semantics.

E / Critics

Establish diverse assignment, commit/reveal reports, quorum, challenge windows, bonds, and proof bundles.

F / Market

Add auctions, bounties, accounting, private tickets, quotas, and abuse controls.

G / Placement

Consider state replication, service discovery, and process placement across browser nodes after storage and evidence hold.

Current progress

Acceptance first

Each surface needs an executable acceptance rule, bounded threat model, and evidence someone else can inspect. Distributed storage and delivery come before claiming that coordinated processes span browser nodes.
